paper.title: Regime-Closure Epistemology (RCE): A General Principle of Cross-Domain Validation in Coupled Multi-Scale Systems
paper.author: Morten Magnusson

rce_principle.description: Five joint conditions for valid cross-domain validation in coupled multi-scale systems

conditions.name: regime_locality
conditions.description: Each subsystem must be validated within its own regime boundaries

conditions.name: variety_closure_ashby
conditions.description: The regulator (model) variety must equal or exceed the system variety (Ashby 1956)

conditions.name: modelling_closure_conant_ashby
conditions.description: The model must be a good regulator of the system: R = I(M;S)/H(S) >= 1 - epsilon (Conant-Ashby 1970)

conditions.name: frozen_parameter_governance
conditions.description: Parameters fixed in one regime must remain frozen when evaluated in another regime

conditions.name: external_arbitration_beer
conditions.description: Validation requires sealed predictions judged by an external arbiter (Beer 1972)

dark_x_diagnostic.description: Normalised ledger gap; if delta > delta_crit the methodology is producing a dark-X artefact

falsification.description: Five falsification conditions stated for the RCE principle itself

preregistered_predictions.description: Seven pre-registered cross-domain predictions with explicit thresholds and arbiters, deposited against the paper DOI

coupling_operator.equation: phi_ij(x) = alpha_ij * x * exp(-|tau_i - tau_j| / tau_bridge)

parameters.alpha_ij: coupling strength between regime i and j

cybernetic_lineage.Conant_Ashby_1970: Every good regulator of a system must be a model of that system
cybernetic_lineage.Bateson_1972: Steps to an Ecology of Mind
cybernetic_lineage.Beer_1972: Brain of the Firm — external arbitration via sealed predictions
